On The Officials and The Secondary: Wild Card Playoffs - Packers at Cardinals
=============================================================================

by[Brandon Benson](https://www.acmepackingcompany.com/authors/brandon)

Jan 12, 2010, 8:02 AM UTC

*    

That's about the best shot of the facemask penalty (that wasn't called) on Green Bay Packers' QB [Aaron Rodgers](http://www.sbnation.com/nfl/players/1977/Aaron_Rodgers) that I can imagine.

First a congratulations from Aaron Schatz (and indirectly Bill Simmons) [from Football Outsiders](http://footballoutsiders.com/audibles/2010/audibles-line-wild-card-round):

> **Aaron Schatz**: I would like to bow to the [Packers](http://www.sbnation.com/nfl/teams/GBP). As Bill Simmons just pointed out on Twitter, even if they don't pull off a win here, they went down huge early and fought back. The [Patriots](http://www.sbnation.com/nfl/teams/NEP), on the other hand, rolled over and died. Advantage: Packers fans.

And then onto the officials:

> **Aaron Schatz**: I don't mean to take away from a very strong pass rush by Arizona, or the quality of the Arizona offense, but... wasn't that facemask and roughing the passer on Adams? He made that sack by grabbing Rodgers' facemask. It's completely obvious, to the point where Joe Buck SAID "hands to the face" as the play was going on.
> 
> 
> **Doug Farrar**: They also missed a helmet-to-helmet that would have wiped out the holding penalty on [Daryn Colledge](http://www.sbnation.com/nfl/players/1934/Daryn_Colledge). Arizona should be congratulated for pulling the game out, but Scott Green’s crew was truly abysmal today.

My basic take was that the officials did an awful job in this game. The [Cardinals](http://www.sbnation.com/nfl/teams/ARI) got away with more when the official kept the flag in his pocket on the final play of the game. And I still can't believe the play where WR Larry Fitzgerald shoved CB [Charles Woodson](http://www.sbnation.com/nfl/players/1991/Charles_Woodson) down in the end zone. But the Cardinals also got hit with two questionable horse collar 15 yard penalties. It was the worst officiated game I've seen all season, even if the Packers took the brunt of it.

I apologize but my "day" job has me working 8am to 11pm this week. My plan had been to re-watch the game and do an extensive play-by-play recap, but I don't have the time right now. But I expect to be talking about this game all offseason because it, along with the loss to the [Steelers](http://www.sbnation.com/nfl/teams/PIT) and the earlier losses to the [Vikings](http://www.sbnation.com/nfl/teams/MIN), are how you beat the Packers: you attack the secondary and win a shootout. Even in their two other losses vs. the [Bengals](http://www.sbnation.com/nfl/teams/CIN) and [Buccaneers](http://www.sbnation.com/nfl/teams/TAM), they surrendered 3 TD passes in each game. Overall the secondary was great this season, but they were a weak link in all 6 losses.

If anyone has something on their mind about the game, please consider writing a Fan Post. I’m checking in periodically during the day, and I’d love to promote a Fan Post to the front page. Thanks.

Nov. 19, 2015Updated Jan. 11, 2016, 11:07 a.m. MT

![Image 1: Cardinals coach Ken Whisenhunt celebrates with fans after beating the Philadelphia Eagles to win the NFC Championship Game at University of Phoenix Stadium in  Glendale on Sunday,  Jan. 18, 2009.](https://www.azcentral.com/gcdn/-mm-/77c65df843cc0cf7594588892bf003cb73812357/c=0-0-3197-1806/local/-/media/2015/11/19/Phoenix/Phoenix/635835396519527527-cardinals-100.jpg?width=660&height=373&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)

_This story was originally published Nov. 20, 2015_.

It’s a number that’s somewhat contrived and yet every single bit as real and important as the fact that the Cardinals are the only team in the NFL that ranks among the league’s top five in both total offense (No. 1) and  total defense (No. 3).

It’s the streaking team’s consecutive sellout streak at University of Phoenix Stadium, which will reach 100 in a row on Sunday night when the [Cardinals (7-2) host the Bengals (8-1)](https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nfl/cardinals/2015/11/18/arizona-cardinals-vs-cincinnati-bengals-tv-radio-stadium-information/76011940/) in their second straight prime-time appearance on NBC.

Even though the “streak” includes preseason games and is based on the premise of “all tickets sold” when there clearly are pockets of empty seats visible in Glendale from game to game, it’s an impressive number nonetheless – 100.

In recognition of reaching the century mark in the stadium’s 10th year of existence, azcentral sports NFL writer [Bob McManaman](http://www.azcentral.com/staff/16937/bob-mcmanaman/) offers his top memories and moments, ranked 1 to 100:

[Cardinals XTRA app: Get the latest news, analysis, scores, more](https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nfl/cardinals/2014/10/03/azcentral-sports-cardinals-xtra-app-iphone/16675731/?from=global)

[![Image 2](https://www.azcentral.com/gcdn/-mm-/a5076e7a43a0cec6129489319d0fb728e2cd1814/c=0-264-5184-3193/local/-/media/2015/11/19/Phoenix/Phoenix/635835344870404445-astadium01.jpg?width=660&height=372&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)](https://www.azcentral.com/picture-gallery/sports/nfl/cardinals/2015/11/19/university-of-phoenix-stadium-memories-moments/76051378/)**1 –** You never forget your first and the first “real” game at the stadium was played Sept. 10, 2006, when the Cardinals beat the 49ers 34-27 as Kurt Warner passed for 301 yards and three touchdowns. Coach Dennis Green gave the game ball to owner Bill Bidwill, telling him, “This is the first of many wins in a building everybody is real proud of.”

**2 –** The biggest game the Cardinals have played there had to be the 2009 NFC Championship against the Eagles, which Arizona won 32-25 to advance to Super Bowl XLIII. Coach Ken Whisenhunt celebrated by taking a victory lap around the place, high-fiving fans for a good five minutes.

**3 –** As in No. 3, quarterback Carson Palmer. He’s 20-4 in his past 24 starts, including 11-2 at University of Phoenix Stadium, since Week 8 of the 2013 season.

**4-5 –** Number of times, if memory serves, that my computer crashed during a Cardinals home game in Glendale.

**6 –** Speaking of crashes, how about Denny Green’s epic "Monday Night Meltdown"? The Bears committed _six_ turnovers against the Cardinals on Oct. 17, 2006, and the Cardinals blew a 23-3 lead in losing 24-23 and Green blew his stack. “The Bears are who we thought they were! That’s why we took the damn field!,” Green screamed in his postgame news conference, before slamming the podium and adding, “Now if you want to crown them, then crown their ass! But they are who we thought they were and we let ’em off the hook!”

[Arizona Cardinals podcast: The Bird's Eye View from Kent Somers and Mike Jurecki](https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nfl/cardinals/2015/09/09/arizona-cardinals-podcast-birds-eye-view-kent-somers-and-mike-jurecki/71954330/?from=global)

**7 –** Number of times I’ve seen the Rolling Stones in concert, including Nov. 8, 2006, at University of Phoenix Stadium, which ranks as one of the best. Thank you, too, Alice Cooper!

**8-11 –** Number of times, give or take, that at least one of the two – or both – press box elevators quit working during or after a game. I was trapped only once, though.

**12 –** Overtime games played by the Cardinals since the stadium opened and 10 of them occurred in Glendale with Arizona winning eight of them. It’s also where Larry Fitzgerald will rank on the NFL’s all-time receptions list if he gets nine catches against the Bengals Sunday night to move ahead of Randy Moss (982).

**13 –** As in No. 13, quarterback Kurt Warner. He spent his final five NFL seasons with the Cardinals from 2005-09, helped take the team to a Super Bowl, and was inducted into the team’s Ring of Honor on Sept. 8, 2014, during a home game against the Chargers.

**14-23 –** Number of fights, at least, that I can recall breaking out in the stands. People, you’ve got to learn to chill. It’s just _football_.

**NFL power rankings: Respecting the Cardinals**

[![Image 3](https://www.azcentral.com/gcdn/-mm-/a41e25ea00f6b570431c93ec3c4c1320b02c5fd7/c=0-0-5034-2844/local/-/media/2015/11/17/Phoenix/Phoenix/635833602798820790-aaanfl01.jpg?width=660&height=372&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)](https://www.azcentral.com/picture-gallery/sports/nfl/2015/11/17/nfl-power-rankings-where-teams-stand-after-week-10/75930078/)**24 –** As in No. 24, safety Adrian Wilson. Pound-for-pound, one of the toughest players to ever strap it on for the Big Red. Wilson was inducted into the Cardinals’ Ring of Honor earlier this season during a Sept. 27 home game against the 49ers.

**25 –** On Jan. 10, 2011, Cam Newton and the Auburn Tigers beat the Oregon Ducks 22-19 in the BCS National Championship game. Wes Byrum’s 19-yard field goal as time expired won it for Auburn. I covered the game from an auxiliary press table situated in the stands, surrounded by thousands of angry Ducks fans who distracted me all night. I made deadline with exactly 25 seconds to spare.

**26-34 –** Number of times I believe Matt Leinart told us he was a leader and had the confidence to be a franchise quarterback. The former first-round pick wound up just starting 17 games for the Cardinals, going 7-10 before he ultimately was released.

**35 –** As in No. 35, cornerback Aeneas Williams. He was inducted into the team’s Ring of Honor on Nov. 10, 2008, during a home game against the 49ers and six years later, was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

**36-39 –** Number of times I’ve secretly wanted to press the button that rolls in the retractable field on game day. Did you know it takes only 65 seconds to move the 18.9 million-pound tray into place?

[Arizona Cardinals' Palmer: Bengals is 'not just another game'](https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nfl/cardinals/2015/11/18/arizona-cardinals-palmer-not-just-another-game/76019632/)

**40 –** As in No. 40, the late great Pat Tillman. The former Arizona State standout set a Cardinals single-season record with 224 tackles in 2000 and would later turn down a three-year contract offer to enlist in the U.S. Army and join the elite Army Ranger unit. He was killed by friendly fire in Afghanistan on April 22, 2004. The Cardinals retired his number, inducted him into their Ring of Honor and an 8-foot, 500-pound white bronze statue of Tillman is the centerpiece of the Pat Tillman Freedom Plaza located on the northwest side of the stadium.

**41 –** Number of 100-yard receiving games by Fitzgerald, 18 of which have come at University of Phoenix Stadium. It also will be the number of career 300-yard passing games by Palmer, if he throws for 300 or more Sunday night at home against the Bengals, his former team.

**42 –** As in Super Bowl XLII in Glendale, when David Tyree made a leaping, one-handed catch that he pinned against his helmet, helping the Giants beat the Patriots 17-14 and end New England’s hopes of becoming the first team to finish a season 19-0. The game is among the greatest upsets in sports history.

**43-48 –** Number of times, I’m guessing, during his final season as coach in 2012 when Whisenhunt gave us a dirty look for asking a question he didn’t like.

**49 –** As in Super Bowl XLIX in Glendale, when against all conventional wisdom, the Seahawks elected to pass the ball with 26 seconds remaining from the Patriots’ 1-yard line instead of calling a run play for Marshawn Lynch. We all know how that ended.

[Arizona Cardinals banged up as Bengals game nears](https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nfl/cardinals/2015/11/18/arizona-cardinals-banged-up-bengals-game-nears/76023680/)

**50-63 –** Number of times, give or take, that Bruce Arians has made us crack up during his always-entertaining news conferences since becoming coach in 2013.

**64 –** The amount of time it took in seconds for quarterback Derek Anderson to go on his own Monday night meltdown during a postgame exchange with colleague Kent Somers. Anderson went on a profanity-laced tirade when Somers asked him why he was laughing on the sideline during a blowout loss to the visiting 49ers on Nov. 30, 2010.

**65 –** Receptions this year by Fitzgerald, which represents the most in his career through the first nine games of a season. His 836 receiving yards and seven touchdowns rank as the second-best totals of his career through nine games.

**66 –** The most sacks by a Cardinals player (Freddie Joe Nunn), a record that one day will belong to Calais Campbell, who is 22 away from breaking it and probably already _should_ have if you listen to Arians.

**67 –** Years it’s been since the Cardinals scored close to this many points (302) through their first nine games of a season. The 1948 team scored 301.

**Rewind: Cardinals show what they are made of**

[![Image 4](https://www.azcentral.com/gcdn/-mm-/0e7c14964c34b48e3ac83655f3287dd661919eec/c=0-0-4037-2281/local/-/media/2015/11/16/Phoenix/Phoenix/635832627495078910-cardinals01.jpg?width=660&height=372&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)](https://www.azcentral.com/picture-gallery/sports/nfl/cardinals/2015/11/16/what-we-learned-in-cardinals-win-over-seahawks/75862664/)**68-74 –** Number of times I’ve probably watched the replay on YouTube of Karlos Dansby returning an Aaron Rodgers fumble 17 yards for a touchdown during the Cardinals’ wild 51-45 NFC wild-card overtime win over the Packers on Jan 10, 2010. It was the highest-scoring playoff game in NFL history and Dansby celebrated his game-winning TD by doing his famous “Dirty Bird” dance in the end zone. It’s almost as good as that crazy Drew Stanton sideline dance last Sunday in Seattle.

**75 –** Length of John Brown’s longest of his four game-winning touchdown receptions for the Cardinals during his rookie season in 2014. They are the most by a rookie in NFL history and yes, all four of them came at University of Phoenix Stadium.

**76-82 –** Estimated number of shoes, including cleats, sneakers, flip-flops, sandals and slippers, that Cardinals star defensive backs and good friends Patrick Peterson and Tyrann Mathieu keep in their lockers. Seriously, it’s true.

**83 –** That’s the jersey number worn by little-known Stephen Spach and if it wasn’t for the tight end out of Fresno State in the 2009 playoffs, the Cardinals may not have made it to the Super Bowl that season. Facing a 3rd-and-16 from the Falcons’ 46-yard line with 2:17 to play, Spach caught a 23-yard pass from Warner that allowed Arizona to run out the clock and advance to the NFC divisional round against Carolina.

**84-89 –** Number of times reporters had to rewrite their game stories during the 2011 season when the Cardinals set an NFL record by playing in four overtime games – all at University of Phoenix Stadium and all wins for Arizona – in addition to authoring six fourth-quarter comeback victories, one shy of the league record.

[Bengals' Andy Dalton, Cardinals' Carson Palmer seek to shed playoff jinx](https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nfl/cardinals/2015/10/16/cincinnati-bengals-andy-dalton-arizona-cardinals-carson-palmer-seek-shed-playoff-jinx/74064834/)

**90 –** As in No. 90, defensive tackle Darnell Dockett, whose last day in a Cardinals uniform sadly came toward the end of training camp, 2014, when he tore his ACL during a stupid, noncontact drill.

**91-98 –** Number of pregame meals in the press box I’m assuming the average media person has devoured over 10 years of covering games in Glendale. (Doesn’t include halftime hot dogs and nachos.)

**99 –** Length in yards of Patrick Peterson’s punt return for a touchdown against the Rams on Nov. 6, 2011, at University of Phoenix Stadium. Peterson returned four punts for TDs that season, becoming just the second rookie to do it and the only player to score all four on returns of at least 80 yards.

**100 –** Consecutive sellouts and you’ll see it, hear it and feel it come Sunday night.

[Cardinals fans must adopt a healthier attitude](https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/heat-index/2015/11/16/cardinals-fans-must-adopt-healthier-attitude/75879620/)

_Reach McManaman at bob.mcmanaman@arizonarepublic.com. Follow him on Twitter @azbobbymac and listen to him live every Monday at 5:30 p.m. on NBC Sports Radio 1060-AM with Roc and Manuch and every Wednesday night between 7-9 p.m. on Fox Sports 910-AM on The Freaks with Kenny and Crash._
